items.case: signing.nk and signing.pub are both missing
items.text:
error: signing.nk and signing.pub are missing from <dir>
hint: mashctl init --config <file>
items.note: From ctl #1390. The signing refusals print in the specification's error rule: `error: <what>` then `hint: <command>`, on stderr, exit 1. <dir> is the key folder as the error carries it (the plain path). The public keys the earlier text printed are not in default output. They are left out of --json too: the error object has only `error` and `hint`, and cliframe has no detail slot for errors. Printed by every mashctl command that signs (endpoint create, reissue, delete) and by init for the first two cases.

items.where: mashctl, a global option before the verb
items.note: mashctl accepts global options before the verb, as mash does (today: error: unknown command "--json"). The result is exactly that of mashctl status --json. The rule "Options go anywhere after the tool's name" already says so; the code does not yet.

items.where: mash, a command that does not exist
items.note: One form in both tools: error: unknown command "nope" (today mash says "mash has no command nope"; mashctl already says this). No hint: a hint is a command that fixes the problem (ADR 0168), and none fixes a misspelt command.

items.where: mashctl endpoint show, suspend, resume, set, unset, inbox, permissions, delete: an address with no record
items.text:
error: no endpoint acme.demo.dave
hint: mashctl endpoint list
items.note: The not-found form of both tools, "no endpoint <address>". Unchanged for mashctl (it already says this); written out so that the other tools' wording is held to it. Exit 1.

items.where: mashctl endpoint reissue: an address with no record
items.text:
error: no endpoint acme.demo.dave
hint: mashctl endpoint list
items.note: Today this reads "acme.demo.dave does not exist"; one not-found form instead. The hint is the one for every not-found: list shows what exists. Exit 1.

rules_next.detail: Always an object, never a bare array: a list is {"endpoints": [...]}. It is the same object the matching MCP tool returns as its structured result. Field names are the glossary's words. Both are produced by one implementation. One policy in both tools: it is indented when standard output is a terminal and one compact line when standard output is a pipe or a file, as gh and aws do. An error object follows the same policy. The specification shows the indented form.

rules_next.rule: In --json, one name for one fact
rules_next.detail: A yes-or-no fact has one name in every command of both tools: online is a boolean wherever it appears (mash who, mash status, mashctl endpoint list and show, mashctl status), never ready, ok or state for the same fact; an endpoint's suspended state is its own boolean, suspended. ready stays the name of "mail works for this endpoint" and "the server works" (mash status and mashctl status, which was ok). A count is named as a count: endpoint_count, online_count, wake_count. An unset field is null: never "" and never left out, so a command's keys are the same on every run. An empty list is [] and an empty map is {}. A list's key is plural: capabilities, not capability, everywhere except mash who --json, whose capability ADR 0049 keeps (who JSON fields are added, never renamed or removed); that is the one named exception. A doctor row's state (ok, warn, fail, skip) is a different fact and keeps its name.

rules_next.rule: A list is a plain table
rules_next.detail: A header row in capitals, two spaces between columns, no borders. Every cell is printed on every row, so a line stands on its own and can be grepped or cut: a repeated owner or group is not left blank. A sender or an endpoint is always its full address. --wide adds columns, and may show the address in place of NAME where both would not fit in 80 (the address carries the name). When an address is long, a line may be longer than 80 columns: nothing is truncated or wrapped, so every line stays one record that grep and cut can use. The 80-column limit applies to the demo's example addresses. Example, at the 64-character maximum: Bob's address northwindtraders.platformengineering.nightlypullrequestreviewers (owner.group.name, 64 characters) is printed whole in the address column of mash inbox and of mashctl endpoint list, and those lines pass 80 columns with nothing cut. An empty list is one sentence.
rules_next.replaces: A list is a plain table

rules_next.detail: Past tense, naming the thing, with a capital first letter and no full stop, in both tools: 'Created endpoint acme.demo.bob', 'Deleted endpoint acme.demo.bob', 'Mail sent (number 42)'. It does not print what another command already shows; it does print an identifier the person can get nowhere else, and the location of a file it wrote ('Credentials: <path>').

rules_next.rule: One thing is a list of 'label: value' lines
rules_next.detail: In every block of such lines, in text and under --detail, the labels are padded to the longest label in the block plus one space, so the values start in one column, and no value begins before it.
rules_next.replaces: One thing is a list of 'label: value' lines

rules_next.rule: A wrong command line gets one error line in a fixed form, and one hint
rules_next.detail: A missing argument: 'error: mash send needs <address>'. A bad value: 'error: --kind must be one of blocker, question, task, result, fyi' or 'error: --reply-to must be a whole number'. Two things that cannot go together: 'error: mash send takes the message text or --file, not both'. A command that does not exist: 'error: unknown command "nope"', in both tools. A flag that does not exist: 'error: unknown flag --x', in both tools, wherever it stands, with no hint (ADR 0168: a hint is a command that fixes the problem, or there is none). Where there is a hint it is a command that fixes the problem, not a pointer to --help. Exit 2, and nothing is attempted.
rules_next.replaces: A wrong command line gets one error line in a fixed form, and one hint

rules_next.detail: 'error: no <thing> <value>', echoing the value as typed: 'error: no endpoint acme.demo.dave', 'error: no message 9'. The hint, when there is one, is the command that lists what exists or makes it.

rules_next.rule: --help has one layout, generated from this specification
rules_next.detail: For a command, in this order: the one-line description; 'Usage:' and the synopsis; 'Examples:'; 'Arguments:'; 'Options:'; 'Global options:'. Nothing else, 80 columns. For the tool itself: its one-line description, then one sentence that says what SAP, NATS and creds are (here and in no other help), then, for mash, one heading per group in the specification's order ('Everyday:', 'Setup:', 'Integration:', 'Raw SAP:') with each command and its one-line description indented beneath; mashctl's top-level help stays one flat list of its verbs in 0.5.10 (grouping it is not part of this item); then 'Global options:' in both tools, followed only by the configuration text that help already carries. A command is described once, in the specification, and that one description is used wherever the command is listed. Help is never written by hand beside the specification.
rules_next.replaces: --help has one layout, generated from this specification
